messages:
anne: Heads up — noticed a weird sequence where the gateway picks backup-model v2 instead of v1 during capacity-shedding and strips X-Client-Route header. Happens when tenant quota dips and CB is in soft-open.
samir: Ugh. Do you have the route config? Could be header normalization ordering in the matcher.
anne: Pasting snippet from the route we hit:
anne: ```
match: prefix:/api/v1/generate
headers:
  X-Client-Route: exact
fallback:
  - model: redwood/bison-v1
    priority: high
  - model: redwood/bison-v2-quant
    priority: low
circuit_breaker:
  max_concurrent: 40
  soft_open_threshold: 0.8
  action: downgrade
```
kevin: That config looks fine; the stripping sounds like a header rewrite happening in the proxy layer. We added an aggressive header-sanitizer in the proxy upgrade last week.
maya: @samir can you check telemetry? I want to see sequence: quota signal -> cb soft-open -> route downgrade -> header mutation.
samir: Pulling traces now. I see the quota-service emits a tenant.backoff event, gateway applies a lane switch, then we hit a path transform in edge-proxy v1.9. Example trace id: trace/0xabc123
ops-bot: quota-service: tenant.backoff emitted for tenant_id=acme-42, rate=0.3
deploy-bot: deploy: edge-proxy v1.9 rolled out to prod/us-west at 2026-03-18T10:12:00Z
kevin: Confirmed: header-sanitizer has a rule that drops unknown headers during lane-switch to legacy lanes. It was meant to prevent leakage for old model variants.
anne: Problem: dropping X-Client-Route breaks our affinity scoring and causes fallback priority tie-breaking to prefer v2 (which includes a backend header check). So it's a functional regression.
maya: Two-prong ask: 1) quick mitigation: exclude X-Client-Route from sanitizer for internal lanes, 2) longer-term: make fallback selection use tenant affinity when present and treat missing header as "preserve route affinity" not default to v2.
samir: Agree. Quick patch to sanitizer is trivial. I'll open a canary patch for edge-proxy and deploy to staging.
kevin: For longer term, maybe fallback selection should include a weighted score: model_score = priority_weight + affinity_bonus + recent_success_rate. That avoids brittle header presence checks.
anne: Also need better telemetry: log whether header was present pre- and post-proxy in the route trace. Right now we only log final model chosen.
samir: Adding that to the tracing spec now. Also will emit a cb.trigger_reason tag when circuit breaker moves to soft-open.
maya: UX note for Console: when a rollout toggles a new proxy rule, surface a warning in the rollout changelist if it affects header sanitation or header policies.
kevin: +1. That would have caught this in the canary review.
anne: Temp plan: @samir patch sanitizer to whitelist X-Client-Route for internal lanes -> canary -> watch telemetry for header preservation and fallback choice -> revert if issues.
samir: Starting on patch. ETA 45m for canary.
kevin: I'll sketch the model_score change and run a simulation on historical routing events this afternoon.
anne: Thanks team. Please @mention in channel when canary completes. :thumbsup:
